tweets.text: This week, @CBP released monthly operational statistics for May. America’s immigration system was decimated over the last four years. We're working swiftly to rebuild, and it’s going to take time, but the data are clear that we've made great progress. Here’s what the numbers say:
tweets.text_resolved: This week, @CBP released monthly operational statistics for May. America’s immigration system was decimated over the last four years. We're working swiftly to rebuild, and it’s going to take time, but the data are clear that we've made great progress. Here’s what the numbers say:

tweets.text: While encounters tend to be on the rise this time of year, the number of Northern Triangle families and unaccompanied children encountered at the Southwest Border have gone down for the second month in a row, decreasing 31% for family units and 23% for unaccompanied children.
tweets.text_resolved: While encounters tend to be on the rise this time of year, the number of Northern Triangle families and unaccompanied children encountered at the Southwest Border have gone down for the second month in a row, decreasing 31% for family units and 23% for unaccompanied children.

tweets.text: The number of total encounters along the Southwest Border is high, but also can be easily misinterpreted. 37% of individuals encountered in May had at least one prior encounter in the last year. From 2014 to 2019, it was 15%.
tweets.text_resolved: The number of total encounters along the Southwest Border is high, but also can be easily misinterpreted. 37% of individuals encountered in May had at least one prior encounter in the last year. From 2014 to 2019, it was 15%.

tweets.text: Accounting for these repeat encounters, the number of unique new individuals encountered at the Southwest Border in May 2021 was down 17% compared to May 2019.
